_documentation.purpose: Second-grader pass by Claude Opus 4.7 on a stratified 30-item sample drawn from v1.3 (the dataset the main paper analyzes). Addresses the v1.0-vs-v1.3 calibration gap flagged in Limitation 3.
_documentation.sampling: Stratified by category (10 well_known + 10 obscure + 10 post_cutoff) with random.Random(42), drawn from data/responses/qwen3_1_7b/{id}.json. Same RNG seed as the v1.0 sample; the seeded shuffle is deterministic per-category but the v1.3 pools are larger (143/153/488 vs v1.0's smaller pools) so the sampled IDs differ from the v1.0 set.
_documentation.grader: Claude (claude-opus-4-7), reading the (question, gold, model answer) triples and applying the literal text of the judge.py decision rule. Without access to the Qwen judge label until after the labeling was complete.
_documentation.decision_rule: Literal application of judge.py: (1) does the answer contain the gold or an acceptable alternative? -> CORRECT. (2) Otherwise, does the model assert a specific competing fact? -> WRONG. (3) Otherwise (declined, hedged, said event hasn't happened) -> REFUSAL.
_documentation.headline_result: Claude vs Qwen-judge agreement on v1.3: 30/30 = 100% (Cohen's kappa = 1.0). The v1.0 calibration (Claude vs Qwen-judge: 28/30 = 93.3%, kappa = 0.892) thus generalizes upward on the v1.3 distribution. Caveat: the v1.3 sample happens not to contain the 'mixed refusal + wrong sub-claim' boundary cases that drove the v1.0 disagreements (sci_wk_08, sci_pc_05, spo_pc_02); the 30/30 rate validates the judge on the typical v1.3 items but does not by itself rule out boundary-case errors at the same rate as v1.0.
_documentation.human_pass_status: Not yet performed. The independent-human leg on v1.3 remains open.
